question: Can currently Chat-exposed create_commit plus update_ref(force=false), or another exposed lightweight GitHub write primitive, synthesize the Ref-identity plus expected-old-head safety property without generic GraphQL createCommitOnBranch?

observations.connector_create_commit: Observed current Chat GitHub connector schema addresses repository by repository_full_name and takes tree_sha plus parent_sha; it exposes no repository numeric/node identity parameter and no branch expected-head condition.
observations.connector_update_ref: Observed current Chat GitHub connector schema addresses repository by repository_full_name and branch by branch_name, takes target sha and force, and exposes no Ref node-ID target nor expected-old-head argument.
observations.connector_contents_update: Observed current contents update primitive uses repository_full_name/path plus current file blob sha. This is file-content CAS, not repository-incarnation identity plus branch-head CAS.
observations.public_reference_semantics: GitHub REST documentation for Update a reference states that force=false ensures a fast-forward update rather than overwriting work; the endpoint is owner/repo/ref plus target sha and force. It documents conflict/validation responses but no expected-current-head parameter.
observations.public_commit_semantics: GitHub REST documentation for Create a commit takes owner/repo, tree and parent commit SHAs; creating the commit object is separate from moving a branch ref.

finite_model.target_model: Target commit C is a single-parent child of expected head H. force=false accepts only when C is a fast-forward from the current branch head; retry to an already-current C is treated as idempotent/no-op. Wrong-incarnation acceptance means any authoritative branch effect lands in same-name replacement repository I1 when authority was frozen for I0.

assumptions: stale Ref node IDs are never rebound across delete/recreate
mutation checks expected head atomically with the Ref-identity-addressed write

new_narrowing.fixed_incarnation_result: Within the tested single-parent commit model and a fixed repository incarnation, create_commit(parent=H) followed by update_ref(force=false) rejects a sibling concurrent branch advance because C is not a descendant of that sibling head. Thus fast-forward semantics can supply useful same-incarnation conflict rejection in this narrow construction.
new_narrowing.not_exact_head_cas: force=false is an ancestry condition, not equality against an explicitly supplied expected head. It may accept an already-current target on retry, which can be useful for idempotency but is semantically different from expectedHeadOid.
new_narrowing.incarnation_failure: Because both exposed calls re-resolve repository by repository_full_name, a same-name replacement before object creation can receive the whole effect. If recreation occurs between object creation and ref update, a replacement containing copied target Git objects can accept the old target as a fast-forward. After response loss, later retry can also apply the same target to a copied replacement, producing a cross-incarnation duplicate.
new_narrowing.composition_verdict: Current create_commit + update_ref(force=false) does not synthesize the Part134 Ref-node-ID + expected-old-head safety property generically. A separate named-head preflight does not help because the check and mutation are not atomic. File-blob CAS is also insufficient under same-history recreation.

scope_guard: This is a finite synthetic model plus current connector-schema inspection and public GitHub REST documentation observed this invocation. It does not assert undocumented GitHub object-retention/copy behavior, Ref node-ID lifetime/non-reuse, authorization-token behavior, branch-protection semantics, Byzantine safety, or safety for external sinks. The unsafe copied-object traces are adversarial possibility tests, not claims that GitHub automatically copies deleted repositories.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for this bounded modeling/documentation slice
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.rate_limit_behavior: rate-limit interruption is modeled as no effect in the current invocation followed by cross-invocation retry; no same-run wait/backoff is required

minimal_unresolved_children: No currently exposed write primitive in the inspected connector supplies both stable repository/ref incarnation identity and an atomic expected-current-head condition.
Provider-guaranteed stale Ref node-ID rejection/non-rebinding across delete/recreate remains unproven from inspected public documentation.
Detection after a name-addressed write may identify recreation but cannot by itself prove that no wrong-incarnation effect was transiently or durably emitted.
exact_continuation: Part136: execute one bounded pre/post repository-identity sandwich leaf. Hold Parts128-135 fixed. Using only current Chat-exposed GitHub read/write schemas, public GitHub repository identity semantics if needed, and own clean state, test whether reading immutable repository numeric/node identity immediately before and after a name-addressed staged write can convert recreation into a safe fail-closed protocol when the write is explicitly non-authoritative until postcheck. Enumerate recreation before precheck, between precheck and staged write, between staged write and postcheck, after postcheck; copied same-history state; response loss; rate-limit interruption/later retry; and postcheck failure. Distinguish prevention of a wrong authoritative effect from detection of a wrong staging effect. If safety depends on staging being non-authoritative and all external publication occurring only after a later identity-fenced gate, classify that residual publication gate as unresolved rather than accepted. Persist exact tested scope, zero-cost/zero-quota assessment, unresolved child and nonempty continuation; do not execute another leaf in the same invocation.
